content.title: About
content.content: Chicken skin is the edible outer covering of the bird, surrounding the body and wings. When cooked properly it becomes crispy, aromatic, and has a rich meaty flavor. It is commonly used for frying, roasting, and adding depth to broths.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken skin contains more fat than the meat, but a portion of this fat consists of beneficial monounsaturated and polyunsaturated acids.
In many traditional cuisines (e.g., Chinese, Mexican, and South American) crispy skin is considered a delicacy.
During frying the skin releases aromatic compounds that enhance the flavor of the whole dish.
Chicken skin can be used to make gelatinous stocks, sauces, and soups, providing body and taste.

items.title: Collagen source
items.content: The skin is rich in collagen, which supports skin, joint, and connective‑tissue health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It provides B2 (riboflavin) and B3 (niacin), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Healthy fatty acids
items.content: Some of the fats are monounsaturated, which can be heart‑friendly when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken skin contains zinc and iron, essential for immune function and blood formation.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Chicken skin is calorie‑dense; excessive intake may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Cholesterol
items.content: It contains a notable amount of cholesterol, which can be a concern for people with elevated blood lipids.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins found in the skin.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Improperly handled skin can harbor bacteria such as Salmonella; thorough cooking is required.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken skin can be fried until golden, baked in the oven, added to soups and stocks for richness, or used as a crunchy garnish for salads. Before cooking, excess fat can be trimmed if a lower‑calorie option is desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh skin in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 2‑3 days. Frozen skin keeps well for up to 3 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
